docs.title: Delphi Topics
docs.text: This page discusses some topics specific to the Delphi version of the Iceoryx2 API and OOP-style library.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Most API's return a generic type TResult<T, E>, which contains either the result of the API or an error value (similar to Rust's Result type).

You can choose to handle the result yourself by checking the IsOk or IsErr properties before you access the Value (or the Error) property. Or you can just use the Value property without checking for validity first, in which case an exception will be raised in case the result contains an error.

To check for errors yourself:

var NodeResult := TNodeBuilder.New.Create(TServiceType.Ipc);
if (NodeResult.IsOk) then
begin
  var Node := NodeResult.Value;
  { ... continue using Node ... }
end
else
  { Handle error yourself }
  HandleError(NodeResult.Error);

To raise an exception in case of an error:

{ Accessing .Value without checking first may raise an exception }
var Node := TNodeBuilder.New.Create(TServiceType.Ipc).Value;

Errors are always of an enumerated type, depending on context, such as TNodeCreationFailure when creating a node failed. When an exception is raised, it contains the string version of the enumerated value.

docs.title: Memory Management
docs.text:
All Iceoryx2 "classes" are wrapped inside Delphi records. Almost all memory management is automatic: any Iceoryx2 "objects" you create are released automatically when those objects go out of scope. This is accomplished through the use of Custom Managed Records.

Most of the time, you can treat this records as classes: they have methods and properties like regular classes do. You can also check against nil to see of the record is assigned, like you would with regular objects.

There are a couple of situations, most notably when using TWaitSetGuard, where you need to release the object manually before any dependent objects go out of scope. In those cases, you should call the Release method (eg. TWaitSetGuard.Release).

docs.title: Static Strings and Vectors
docs.text:
You cannot communicate Delphi strings or dynamic arrays across processes since these types are basically pointers to dynamically allocated memory. Instead, you can use the TStaticString<> and TStaticVector<> types from the Neslib.Iceoryx2.Containers unit.

The TStaticString<> and TStaticVector<> types are compatible across Delphi, C++ and Rust, and any other language binding that follows the original Rust specification. However, using them in Delphi is a bit more complicated since Delphi doesn't support "generic value parameters". For example, unlike C++ and Rust, in Delphi you cannot declare a static string like this:

var Name: TStaticString<256>;

Instead you need to define a storage type that is 256 bytes in size:

type
  TNameStorage = array [0..255] of Byte;

var Name: TStaticString<TNameStorage>;

Or use one of the pre-defined storage types like T256Bytes.

For TStaticVector<>, the storage specifies the number of bytes, not the number of elements in the vector. So if you want to create a static vector that can hold at most 8 values of type Double, than you need 64 bytes of storage since a Double is 8 bytes in size:

type
  TRow = TStaticVector<Double, T64Bytes>;

Declaring a two dimensional vector (eg. a nested vector or matrix) gets a bit more complicated since you need know how much storage you need for a single row in the matrix. You cannot just multiple the number of rows by the number of columns by the size of each element, since TStaticVector<> itself also adds some overhead. So you need to declare a data type for the storage of the matrix first:

type
  TMatrixStorage = array [0..(8 * SizeOf(TRow)) - 1] of Byte;

You cannot declare TRow and TMatrixStorage in the same type section. Doing so will result in a compilation error.

And then you can declare a matrix like this:

var SomeMatrix: TStaticVector<TRow, TMatrixStorage>;

If you don't define the storage types correctly, then you will get an "Incompatible Types" error when trying to communicate with a service written in a language other than Delphi.

docs.title: TMessagingPattern
docs.text: Supported messaging patterns.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Unit: Neslib.Iceoryx2

type TMessagingPattern = (PublishSubscribe, Event, RequestResponse, Blackboard)

docs.title: PublishSubscribe = _iox2_messaging_pattern_e_PUBLISH_SUBSCRIBE
docs.text: Unidirectional communication pattern where the TPublisher sends arbitrary data to the TSubscriber.

docs.title: Event = _iox2_messaging_pattern_e_EVENT
docs.text: Unidirectional communication pattern where the TNotifier sends signals/events to the TListener which has the ability to sleep until a signal/event arrives. Building block to realize push-notifications.

docs.title: RequestResponse = _iox2_messaging_pattern_e_REQUEST_RESPONSE
docs.text: Bidirectional communication pattern where the TClient sends arbitrary data in form of requests to the TServer and receives a stream of responses.

docs.title: Blackboard = _iox2_messaging_pattern_e_BLACKBOARD
docs.text: Unidirectional communication pattern where the TWriter writes arbitrary data to a key-value store which can be read by many TReader's.

docs.title: BlockingCleanupDeadNodes(TDuration)
docs.text:
Removes the stale system resources of all dead TNode's connected to this service.

If a TNode cannot be cleaned up since the process has insufficient permissions then the TNode is skipped. If it is currently being cleaned up by another process then the cleaner will wait until the timeout as either passed or the cleaned was finished.

The timeout is applied to every individual dead TNode the function needs to wait on.

docs.title: TBlackboardCreateError
docs.text: Errors that can occur when a new TMessagingPattern.Blackboard service shall be created.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Unit: Neslib.Iceoryx2.Blackboard

type TBlackboardCreateError = (Interrupt, AlreadyExists, IsBeingCreatedByAnotherInstance, InternalFailure, InsufficientPermissions, ServiceInCorruptedState, HangsInCreation, NoEntriesProvided, UnableToCreateServiceTag, ServiceConfigCouldNotBeCreated, UnableToGenerateUniqueServiceId)

docs.title: Interrupt (0)
docs.text: An interrupt signal was raised.

docs.title: AlreadyExists (1)
docs.text: The service already exists.

docs.title: IsBeingCreatedByAnotherInstance (2)
docs.text: Multiple processes are trying to create the same service.

docs.title: InternalFailure (3)
docs.text: Errors that indicate either an implementation issue or a wrongly configured system.

docs.title: InsufficientPermissions (4)
docs.text: The process has insufficient permissions to create the service.

docs.title: ServiceInCorruptedState (5)
docs.text: Some underlying resources of the service are either missing, corrupted or inaccessible.

docs.title: HangsInCreation (6)
docs.text: The service's creation timeout has passed and it is still not initialized. Can be caused by a process that crashed during service creation.

docs.title: NoEntriesProvided (7)
docs.text: No key-value pairs have been provided. At least one is required.

docs.title: UnableToCreateServiceTag (8)
docs.text: The TNode service tag could not be created. Required to track resources

docs.title: ServiceConfigCouldNotBeCreated (9)
docs.text: The service's config could not be created and written to the static service configuration.

docs.title: UnableToGenerateUniqueServiceId (10)
docs.text: The unique service id could not be generated.

docs.title: TBlackboardOpenError
docs.text: Errors that can occur when an existing TMessagingPattern.Blackboard service shall be opened.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Unit: Neslib.Iceoryx2.Blackboard

type TBlackboardOpenError = (Interrupt, DoesNotExist, ServiceInCorruptedState, IncompatibleKeys, InternalFailure, IncompatibleAttributes, IncompatibleMessagingPattern, DoesNotSupportRequestedAmountOfReaders, InsufficientPermissions, HangsInCreation, IsMarkedForDestruction, ExceedsMaxNumberOfNodes, DoesNotSupportRequestedAmountOfNodes, UnableToCreateServiceTag, VersionMismatch)

docs.title: Interrupt (0)
docs.text: An interrupt signal was raised.

docs.title: DoesNotExist (1)
docs.text: The service could not be opened since it does not exist.

docs.title: ServiceInCorruptedState (2)
docs.text: Some underlying resources of the service are either missing, corrupted or inaccessible.

docs.title: IncompatibleKeys (3)
docs.text: The service has the wrong key type.

docs.title: InternalFailure (4)
docs.text: Errors that indicate either an implementation issue or a wrongly configured system.

docs.title: IncompatibleAttributes (5)
docs.text: The AttributeVerifier required attributes that the service does not satisfy.

docs.title: IncompatibleMessagingPattern (6)
docs.text: The service has the wrong messaging pattern.

docs.title: DoesNotSupportRequestedAmountOfReaders (7)
docs.text: The service supports less TReader's than requested.

docs.title: InsufficientPermissions (8)
docs.text: The process has not enough permissions to open the service

docs.title: HangsInCreation (9)
docs.text: The service's creation timeout has passed and it is still not initialized. Can be caused by a process that crashed during service creation.

docs.title: IsMarkedForDestruction (10)
docs.text: The service is marked for destruction and currently cleaning up since no one is using it anymore. When the call creation call is repeated with a little delay the service should be recreatable.

docs.title: ExceedsMaxNumberOfNodes (11)
docs.text: The maximum number of TNode's have already opened the service.

docs.title: DoesNotSupportRequestedAmountOfNodes (12)
docs.text: The service supports less TNode's than requested.

docs.title: UnableToCreateServiceTag (13)
docs.text: The TNode service tag could not be created. Required to track resources of dead nodes when cleaning them up.

docs.title: VersionMismatch (14)
docs.text: The iceoryx2 service version does not match the one of the service.

docs.title: TStaticString<TStorage>
docs.text: A UTF-8 string with fixed static capacity and contiguous inplace storage. The string class uses Unicode (ISO/IEC 10646) terminology throughout its interface. In particular: - A code point is the numerical index assigned to a character in the Unicode standard. - A code unit is the basic component of a character encoding system. For UTF-8, the code unit has a size of 8-bits For example, the code point U+0041 represents the letter 'A' and can be encoded in a single 8-bit code unit in UTF-8. The code point U+1F4A9 requires four 8-bit code units in the UTF-8 encoding.

The layout of this record is compatible with its C++ and Rust counterparts, so it can be used for cross-language communication.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:

type TServiceBuilderEvent = record ... end;

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Name Description _Init Create Creates a new service. CreateWithAttributes Creates a new service with a set of attributes. Deadline Enables the deadline property of the service. There must be a notification emitted by any TNotifier after at least the provided ADeadline. DisableDeadline Disables the deadline property of the service. TNotifier can signal notifications at any rate. DisableNotifierCreatedEvent If the service is created it disables sending an event when a new notifier was created. DisableNotifierDeadEvent If the service is created it disables sending an event when a notifier was identified as dead DisableNotifierDroppedEvent If the service is created it disables sending an event when a notifier was dropped. EventIdMaxValue If the service is created it set the greatest supported TNodeId value. If an existing service is opened it defines the value size the TNodeId must at least support. MaxListeners If the service is created it defines how many TListener's shall be supported at most. If an existing service is opened it defines how many TListener's must be at least supported. MaxNodes If the service is created it defines how many TNode's shall be able to open it in parallel. If an existing service is opened it defines how many TNode's must be at least supported. MaxNotifiers If the service is created it defines how many TNotifier's shall be supported at most. If an existing service is opened it defines how many TNotifier's must be at least supported. NotifierCreatedEvent If the service is created it defines the event that shall be emitted by every newly created TNotifier. NotifierDeadEvent If the service is created it defines the event that shall be emitted when a TNotifier is identified as dead. If none is provided no event will be emitted. NotifierDroppedEvent If the service is created it defines the event that shall be emitted by every TNotifier before it is dropped. If none is provided a TNotifier will not emit an event. Open Opens an existing service. OpenOrCreate If the service exists, it will be opened otherwise a new service will be created. OpenOrCreateWithAttributes If the service exists, it will be opened otherwise a new service will be created. It defines a set of attributes. If the service already exists, all attribute requirements must be satisfied otherwise the open process will fail. If the service does not exist the required attributes will be defined in the service. OpenWithAttributes Opens an existing service with attribute requirements. If the defined attribute requirements are not satisfied the open process will fail.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Name Description Loan Loans/allocates a TSampleMut from the underlying data segment of the publisher and initialize it with the default value. This can be a performance hit and TPublisher.LoanUninit can be used to loan an uninitialized TSampleMut. LoanSlice Loans/allocates a TSampleMut from the underlying data segment of the TPublisher and initializes all slice elements with the default value. This can be a performance hit and TPublisher.LoanSliceUninit can be used to loan a slice of uninitialized payload. LoanSliceUninit Loans/allocates a TSampleMutUninit from the underlying data segment of the Publisher. The user has to initialize the payload before it can be sent. LoanUninit Loans/allocates a TSampleMutUninit from the underlying data segment of the publisher. The user has to initialize the payload before it can be sent. SendCopy Copies the input value into a TSampleMut and delivers it. On success it returns the number of TSubscriber's that received the data, otherwise a TSendError describing the failure. SendSliceCopy Copies the input APayload slice into a TSampleMut and delivers it. On success it returns the number of TSubscriber's that received the data, otherwise a TSendError describing the failure. UpdateConnections Explicitly updates all connections to the TSubscriber's. This is required to be called whenever a new TSubscriber is connected to the service. It is called implicitly whenever TSampleMut.Send or TPublisher.SendCopy is called. When a TSubscriber is connected that requires a history this call will deliver it.

docs.title: Loan
docs.text:
Loans/allocates a TSampleMut from the underlying data segment of the publisher and initialize it with the default value. This can be a performance hit and TPublisher.LoanUninit can be used to loan an uninitialized TSampleMut.

On failure it returns a TLoanError describing the failure.

docs.title: Type Parameters
docs.text:
TPayload:

TUserHeader:

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Name Description _Init Create Creates a new service. CreateWithAttributes Creates a new service with a set of attributes. EnableSafeOverflow If the service is created, defines the overflow behavior of the service. If an existing service is opened it requires the service to have the defined overflow behavior. HistorySize If the service is created it defines the maximum history size a subscriber can request on connection. If an existing service is opened it defines the minimum required. MaxNodes If the service is created it defines how many nodes shall be able to open it in parallel. If an existing service is opened it defines how many nodes must be at least supported. MaxPublishers If the service is created it defines how many publishers shall be supported at most. If an existing service is opened it defines how many publishers must be at least supported. MaxSubscribers If the service is created it defines how many subscribers shall be supported at most. If an existing service is opened it defines how many subscribers must be at least supported. Open Opens an existing service. OpenOrCreate If the service exists, it will be opened otherwise a new service will be created. OpenOrCreateWithAttributes If the service exists, it will be opened otherwise a new service will be created. It defines a set of attributes. If the service already exists all attribute requirements must be satisfied otherwise the open process will fail. If the service does not exist the required attributes will be defined in the service. OpenWithAttributes Opens an existing service with attribute requirements. If the defined attribute requirements are not satisfied the open process will fail. PayloadAlignment If the service is created, it defines the alignment of the payload for the service. If an existing service is opened it requires the service to have at least the defined alignment. If the payload alignment is greater than the provided alignment then the payload alignment is used. ResumeBuild Returns the builder as an r-value so the fluent chain can be resumed after a free function, such as SetPayloadTypeDetails or SetUserHeaderTypeDetails, has been applied to the named builder. SubscriberMaxBorrowedSamples If the service is created it defines how many samples a subscriber can borrow at most in parallel. If an existing service is opened it defines the minimum required. SubscriberMaxBufferSize If the service is created it defines how many samples a subscriber can store in its internal buffer. If an existing service is opened it defines the minimum required. UserHeader<TNewHeader> Sets the user header type of the service.

docs.text: Errors that can occur when a new TMessagingPattern.PublishSubscribe service shall be created.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Unit: Neslib.Iceoryx2.PublishSubscribe

type TPublishSubscribeCreateError = (Interrupt, ServiceInCorruptedState, SubscriberBufferMustBeLargerThanHistorySize, AlreadyExists, InsufficientPermissions, InternalFailure, IsBeingCreatedByAnotherInstance, HangsInCreation, UnableToCreateServiceTag, ServiceConfigCouldNotBeCreated, UnableToAcquireTypeDefinition, InvalidTypeDefinition, UnableToGenerateUniqueServiceId)

docs.title: Interrupt (0)
docs.text: An interrupt signal was raised.

docs.title: ServiceInCorruptedState (1)
docs.text: Some underlying resources of the service are either missing, corrupted or inaccessible.

docs.title: SubscriberBufferMustBeLargerThanHistorySize (2)
docs.text: Invalid service configuration provided. The subscriber's buffer size must be at least the size of the history. Otherwise, how could it hold the whole history?

docs.title: AlreadyExists (3)
docs.text: The service already exists.

docs.title: InsufficientPermissions (4)
docs.text: The process has insufficient permissions to create the service.

docs.title: InternalFailure (5)
docs.text: Errors that indicate either an implementation issue or a wrongly configured system.

docs.title: IsBeingCreatedByAnotherInstance (6)
docs.text: Multiple processes are trying to create the same service.

docs.title: HangsInCreation (7)
docs.text: The service's creation timeout has passed and it is still not initialized. Can be caused by a process that crashed during service creation.

docs.title: UnableToCreateServiceTag (8)
docs.text: The TNode service tag could not be created. Required to track resources of dead nodes when cleaning them up.

docs.title: ServiceConfigCouldNotBeCreated (9)
docs.text: The service's config could not be created and written to the static service configuration.

docs.title: UnableToAcquireTypeDefinition (10)
docs.text: When using a serialized format such as FlatBuffers, the iceoryx2 service requires the type definition. By default, it uses the lookup path defined in the config. If no type definition file was specified in the service builder and no file could be found, this error is returned.

docs.title: InvalidTypeDefinition (11)
docs.text: When using a serialized format such as Flatbuffers, the iceoryx2 service requires a specific type definition format. If the wrong type definition format was provided, this error is returned.

docs.title: UnableToGenerateUniqueServiceId (12)
docs.text: The unique service id could not be generated.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Name Description AllocationStrategy Defines the allocation strategy that is used when the provided InitialMaxSliceLen is exhausted. This happens when the user acquires more than max slice len in TClient.LoanSlice or TClient.LoanSliceUninit. BackpressureStrategy Sets the TBackpressureStrategy which defines how the TClient shall behave when a TServer cannot receive a TRequestMut since its internal buffer is full. Create Creates a new TClient or returns a TClientCreateError on failure. InitialMaxSliceLen Sets the maximum number of elements that can be loaned in a slice. MaxActiveRequests Defines the required maximal amount of active requests the TClient can send. Smallest possible value is 1. Name The TPortName that shall be assigned to the TClient. It does not have to be unique. If no TPortName is defined then the TClient does not have a name. OverrideRequestPreallocation Defines a callback to reduce the number of preallocated TRequestMut's. The input argument is the worst case number of preallocated TRequestMut's required to guarantee that the TClient never runs out of TRequestMut's to loan and send. The return value is clamped between 1 and the worst case number of preallocated TRequestMut's. SetBackpressureHandler Sets the TBackpressureHandler of the TClient. Whenever a TRequestMut cannot be sent to a TServer, this handler is called and depending on the returned TBackpressureAction, measures will be taken. If no handler is set, the measures will be determined by the value set in TBackpressureStrategy. SetRequestDegradationHandler Sets the TDegradationHandler for sending TRequestMut from the TClient. Whenever a request connection to a TServer is corrupted, this handler is called and depending on the returned TDegradationAction measures will be taken. SetResponseDegradationHandler Sets the TDegradationHandler for receiving TResponse's from a TServer. Whenever a response connection to a TServer is corrupted, this handler is called and depending on the returned TDegradationAction measures will be taken.

docs.text: Name Description AllocationStrategy Defines the allocation strategy that is used when the provided InitialMaxSliceLen is exhausted. Create Creates a new TServer or returns a TServerCreateError on failure. InitialMaxSliceLen Sets the maximum initial slice length configured for this server. MaxLoanedResponsesPerRequest Defines the maximum number of TResponseMut's that the TServer can loan in parallel per TActiveRequest. Name The TPortName that shall be assigned to the TServer. Whenever a request connection to a TClient is corrupted, this handler is called and depending on the returned TDegradationAction measures will be taken. docs.text:
Acquired by a TActiveRequest with TActiveRequest.Loan.

It stores the payload of the response that will be sent to the corresponding PendingResponse of the client.

If the TResponseMut is not sent it will release the loaned memory when going out of scope.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Name Description _Init Create Creates a new service. CreateWithAttributes Creates a new service with a set of attributes. EnableFireAndForgetRequests If the service is created, defines the fire-and-forget behavior of the service for requests. EnableSafeOverflowForRequests If the service is created, defines the overflow behavior of the service for requests. If an existing service is opened it requires the service to have the defined overflow behavior. EnableSafeOverflowForResponses If the service is created, defines the overflow behavior of the service for responses. If an existing service is opened it requires the service to have the defined overflow behavior. MaxActiveRequestsPerClient Defines how many active requests a TServer can hold in parallel per TClient. The objects are used to send answers to a request that was received earlier from a TClient. MaxBorrowedResponsesPerPendingResponse If the service is created it defines how many TResponse's shall be able to be borrowed in parallel per TPendingResponse. If an existing service is opened it defines how many borrows must be at least supported. MaxClients If the service is created it defines how many TClient's shall be supported at most. If an existing service is opened it defines how many TClient's must be at least supported. MaxLoanedRequests If the service is created it defines how many TRequestMut's a TClient can loan in parallel. MaxNodes If the service is created it defines how many TNode's shall be able to open it in parallel. If an existing service is opened it defines how many TNode's must be at least supported. MaxResponseBufferSize If the service is created it defines how many responses fit in the TClients's buffer. If an existing service is opened it defines the minimum required. MaxServers If the service is created it defines how many TServer's shall be supported at most. If an existing service is opened it defines how many TServer's must be at least supported. Open Opens an existing service. OpenOrCreate If the service exists, it will be opened otherwise a new service will be created. OpenOrCreateWithAttributes If the service exists, it will be opened otherwise a new service will be created. It defines a set of attributes. OpenWithAttributes Opens an existing service with attribute requirements. If the defined attribute requirements are not satisfied the open process will fail. RequestPayloadAlignment If the service is created, it defines the request alignment of the payload for the service. If an existing service is opened it requires the service to have at least the defined alignment. If the payload alignment is greater than the provided alignment then the payload alignment is used. RequestUserHeader<TNewRequestUserHeader> Sets the request user header type of the service. ResponsePayloadAlignment If the service is created, it defines the response alignment of the payload for the service. If an existing service is opened it requires the service to have at least the defined alignment. If the payload alignment is greater than the provided alignment then the payload alignment is used. ResponseUserHeader<TNewResponseUserHeader> Sets the response user header type of the servic]. ResumeBuild Returns the builder as an r-value so the fluent chain can be resumed after a free function, such as SetRequestHeaderTypeDetails or SetRequestPayloadTypeDetails, has been applied to the named builder.

docs.title: UnableToCreateDataSegment (0)
docs.text: The datasegment in which the payload of the client is stored, could not be created.

docs.title: ExceedsMaxSupportedClients (1)
docs.text: The maximum amount of clients that can connect to a service is defined in TConfig. When this is exceeded no more clients can be created for a specific service.

docs.title: FailedToDeployThreadsafetyPolicy (2)
docs.text: Caused by a failure when instantiating a ArcSyncPolicy defined in the service as ArcThreadSafetyPolicy.

docs.title: UnableToCreatePortTag (3)
docs.text: The tracking port tag, required for cleanup, could not be created.

docs.title: MaxActiveRequestsExceedsMaxSupportedActiveRequestsOfService (4)
docs.text: When the client requires more active requests than the service offers, the creation will fail.

docs.title: UnableToGenerateUniqueClientId (5)
docs.text: The UniqueClientId could not be generated.

type TRequestResponseCreateError = (Interrupt, AlreadyExists, InternalFailure, IsBeingCreatedByAnotherInstance, InsufficientPermissions, HangsInCreation, ServiceInCorruptedState, UnableToCreateServiceTag, ServiceConfigCouldNotBeCreated, UnableToAcquireTypeDefinition, InvalidTypeDefinition, UnableToGenerateUniqueServiceId)

docs.title: Interrupt (0)
docs.text: An interrupt signal was raised.

docs.text: The service already exists.

docs.title: InternalFailure (2)
docs.text: Errors that indicate either an implementation issue or a wrongly configured system.

docs.title: IsBeingCreatedByAnotherInstance (3)
docs.text: Multiple processes are trying to create the same service.

docs.text: The process has insufficient permissions to create the service.

docs.text: The services creation timeout has passed and it is still not initialized. Can be caused by a process that crashed during service creation.

docs.text: Some underlying resources of the service are either missing, corrupted or inaccessible.

docs.title: UnableToCreateServiceTag (7)
docs.text: The TNode service tag could not be created. Required to track resources of dead nodes when cleaning them up.

docs.title: PRefCountedHandle
docs.text:
A shared reference count for a handle to an underlying C object. These are very cheap to allocate and don't cause memory fragmentation.

These are not thread safe! Different handles can be used in different threads, but once created inside a thread, they can only be used from that thread. This is check with assertions.

docs.text: Name Description BlockingRemoveStaleResources Removes all stale resources of a dead TNode. docs.title: BlockingRemoveStaleResources(TDuration)
docs.text:
Removes all stale resources of a dead TNode. If another instance is already removing the dead TNode it waits until the other instance has cleaned up the dead TNode completely. If the other cleanup instance crashes, it will take over the ownership and continue the cleanup. If the process does not have the permission to cleanup all resources it aborts with an error.

If the provided timeout is expired it will return with TNodeCleanupFailure.AnotherInstanceIsCleaningUp.

SubscriberMaxBorrowedSamples The maximum amount of TSample's a TSubscriber can hold at the same time. SubscriberMaxBufferSize The maximum buffer size a TSubscriber can have

docs.title: TConfig.TRequestResponse
docs.text: Default settings for the request response messaging pattern. These settings are used unless the user specifies custom QoS or port settings.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Unit: Neslib.Iceoryx2.Types

type TRequestResponse = record ... end;

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Name Description ClientBackpressureStrategy Defines the TBackpressureStrategy when a TClient could not deliver the request to the TServer. ClientExpiredConnectionBuffer Defines the size of the internal TClient buffer that contains expired connections. A connection is expired when the TServer disconnected from a service and the connection still contains unconsumed TResponse's. EnableFireAndForgetRequests Allows the TServer to receive TRequestMut's of TClient's that are not interested in a TResponse, meaning that the TServer will receive the TRequestMut despite the corresponding TPendingResponse already went out-of-scope. So any TResponse sent by the TServer would not be received by the corresponding TClient's TPendingResponse. EnableSafeOverflowForRequests Defines if the request buffer of the service safely overflows. EnableSafeOverflowForResponses Defines if the response buffer of the service safely overflows. MaxActiveRequestsPerClient The maximum of TActiveRequest's a TServer can hold in parallel per TClient. MaxBorrowedResponsesPerPendingResponse The maximum amount of borrowed TResponse's per TPendingResponse on the TClient side. MaxClients The maximum amount of supported TClient's. MaxLoanedRequests Defines how many TRequestMut's a TClient can loan in parallel. MaxNodes The maximum amount of supported TNode's. Defines indirectly how many processes can open the service at the same time. MaxResponseBufferSize The maximum buffer size for TResponse's for a TPendingResponse. MaxServers The maximum amount of supported TServer's. ServerBackpressureStrategy Defines the TBackpressureStrategy when a TServer could not deliver the response to the TClient. ServerExpiredConnectionBuffer Defines the size of the internal TServer buffer that contains expired connections. A connection is expired when the TClient disconnected from a service and the connection still contains unconsumed TActiveRequest's. ServerMaxLoanedResponsesPerRequest Defines how many TResponseMut's a TServer can loan in parallel per TActiveRequest.

docs.title: EnableFireAndForgetRequests
docs.text:
Allows the TServer to receive TRequestMut's of TClient's that are not interested in a TResponse, meaning that the TServer will receive the TRequestMut despite the corresponding TPendingResponse already went out-of-scope. So any TResponse sent by the TServer would not be received by the corresponding TClient's TPendingResponse.

Consider enabling this feature if you do not want to loose any TRequestMut.

property EnableFireAndForgetRequests: Boolean read GetEnableFireAndForgetRequests write SetEnableFireAndForgetRequests

Type: Boolean

docs.title: TAllocationStrategy
docs.text: Describes generically an allocation strategy, meaning how the memory is increased when the available memory is insufficient.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Unit: Neslib.Iceoryx2.Types

type TAllocationStrategy = (BestFit, PowerOfTwo, &Static)

docs.title: BestFit = _iox2_allocation_strategy_e_BEST_FIT
docs.text: Increases the memory so that it perfectly fits the new size requirements. This may lead to a lot of reallocations but has the benefit that no byte is wasted.

docs.title: PowerOfTwo = _iox2_allocation_strategy_e_POWER_OF_TWO
docs.text: Increases the memory by rounding the increased memory size up to the next power of two. Reduces reallocations a lot at the cost of increased memory usage.

docs.title: &Static = _iox2_allocation_strategy_e_STATIC
docs.text: The memory is not increased. This may lead to an out-of-memory error when allocating.

docs.text: Name Description TWaitSet The TWaitSet implements a reactor pattern and allows to wait on multiple events in one single call (TWaitSet.WaitAndProcessOnce) until it wakes up or to run repeatedly with (TWaitSet.WaitAndProcess) until an interrupt or termination signal was received or the user has explicitly requested to stop by returning TCallbackProgression.Stop in the provided callback. TWaitSetAttachmentId TWaitSetBuilder The builder for the TWaitSet. TWaitSetGuard The TWaitSetGuard is returned by TWaitSet.AttachDeadline, TWaitSet.AttachNotification or TWaitSet.AttachInterval. As soon as it goes out-of-scope it detaches the attachment. It can also be used to determine the origin of an event in TWaitSet.WaitAndProcess or TWaitSet.WaitAndProcessOnce via TWaitSetAttachmentId.HasEventFrom or TWaitSetAttachmentId.HasMissedDeadline.

TWaitSetCreateError Defines the failures that can occur when calling TWaitSetBuilder.Create. TWaitSetRunError Defines the failures that can occur when calling TWaitSet.Run. TWaitSetRunResult States why the TWaitSet.Run method returned.

docs.title: TWaitSet
docs.text:
The TWaitSet implements a reactor pattern and allows to wait on multiple events in one single call (TWaitSet.WaitAndProcessOnce) until it wakes up or to run repeatedly with (TWaitSet.WaitAndProcess) until an interrupt or termination signal was received or the user has explicitly requested to stop by returning TCallbackProgression.Stop in the provided callback.

The TListener can be attached as well as sockets or anything else that can be packed into a TFileDescriptorView.

Can be created via the TWaitSetBuilder.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Unit: Neslib.Iceoryx2.WaitSet

type TWaitSet = record ... end;

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Name Description Capacity Returns the capacity of the TWaitSet Count Returns the number of attachments. Handle IsEmpty Returns True if the TWaitSet has no attachments, otherwise False. SignalHandlingMode Returns the TSignalHandlingMode with which the TWaitSet was created.

docs.title: Constructors
docs.text: Name Description Assign Finalize Initialize

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Name Description Equal NotEqual

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Name Description AttachDeadline(TFileDescriptorBased, TDuration) Attaches a TFileDescriptorBased object as deadline to the TWaitSet. Whenever the event is received or the deadline is hit, the user is informed in TWaitSet.WaitAndProcess. The object cannot be attached twice and the TWaitSet.Capacity is limited by the underlying implementation. Whenever the object emits an event the deadline is reset by the TWaitSet. AttachDeadline(TListener, TDuration) Attaches a TListener as deadline to the TWaitSet. Whenever the event is received or the deadline is hit, the user is informed in TWaitSet.WaitAndProcess. The object cannot be attached twice and the TWaitSet.Capacity is limited by the underlying implementation. Whenever the object emits an event the deadline is reset by the TWaitSet. AttachInterval Attaches a tick event to the TWaitSet. Whenever the timeout is reached the TWaitSet informs the user in TWaitSet.WaitAndProcess. AttachNotification(TFileDescriptorBased) Attaches a TFileDescriptorBased object as notification to the TWaitSet. Whenever an event is received on the object the TWaitSet informs the user in TWaitSet.WaitAndProcess to handle the event. The object cannot be attached twice and the TWaitSet.Capacity is limited by the underlying implementation. AttachNotification(TListener) Attaches a TListener as notification to the TWaitSet. Whenever an event is received on the object the TWaitSet informs the user in TWaitSet.WaitAndProcess to handle the event. The object cannot be attached twice and the TWaitSet.Capacity is limited by the underlying implementation. WaitAndProcess Waits until an event arrives on the TWaitSet, then collects all events by calling the provided callback with the corresponding TWaitSetAttachmentId. In contrast to [TWaitSet.WaitAndProcessOnce it will never return until the user explicitly requests it by returning TCallbackProgression.Stop or by receiving a signal. WaitAndProcessOnce Waits until an event arrives on the TWaitSet, then collects all events by calling the provided callback with the corresponding TWaitSetAttachmentId and then returns. This makes it ideal to be called in some kind of event-loop. WaitAndProcessOnceWithTimeout Waits until an event arrives on the TWaitSet or the provided timeout has passed, then collects all events by calling the provided callback with the corresponding TWaitSetAttachmentId and then returns. This makes it ideal to be called in some kind of event-loop.

docs.title: WaitAndProcess(TCallback<TWaitSetAttachmentId>)
docs.text:
Waits until an event arrives on the TWaitSet, then collects all events by calling the provided callback with the corresponding TWaitSetAttachmentId. In contrast to [TWaitSet.WaitAndProcessOnce it will never return until the user explicitly requests it by returning TCallbackProgression.Stop or by receiving a signal.

The provided callback must return TCallbackProgression.Continue to continue the event processing and handle the next event or TCallbackProgression.Stop to return from this call immediately. All unhandled events will be lost forever and the call will return TWaitSetRunResult.StopRequest.

If an interrupt- (SIGINT) or a termination-signal (SIGTERM) was received, it will exit the loop and inform the user with TWaitSetRunResult.Interrupt or TWaitSetRunResult.TerminationRequest.

function WaitAndProcess(const ACallback: TCallback<TWaitSetAttachmentId>): TResult<TWaitSetRunResult, TWaitSetRunError>

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: ACallback: TCallback<TWaitSetAttachmentId>

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: TResult<TWaitSetRunResult, TWaitSetRunError>

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text:
Important: The TWaitSet only reports that an attachment is ready; it does not consume the notification or data that caused the wake-up. If the callback returns without consuming any pending input, the attachment remains ready and the TWaitSet wakes up again immediately. Repeating this can cause a busy loop and high CPU usage.

For a TListener, consume pending notifications with TListener.TryWait. For a socket or another file-descriptor-based attachment, consume the pending data using its corresponding read or receive API.

docs.title: WaitAndProcessOnce(TCallback<TWaitSetAttachmentId>)
docs.text:
Waits until an event arrives on the TWaitSet, then collects all events by calling the provided callback with the corresponding TWaitSetAttachmentId and then returns. This makes it ideal to be called in some kind of event-loop.

The provided callback must return TCallbackProgression.Continue to continue the event processing and handle the next event or TCallbackProgression.Stop to return from this call immediately. All unhandled events will be lost forever and the call will return TWaitSetRunResult.StopRequest.

If an interrupt- (SIGINT) or a termination-signal (SIGTERM) was received, it will exit the loop and inform the user with TWaitSetRunResult.Interrupt or TWaitSetRunResult.TerminationRequest.

When no signal was received and all events were handled, it will return TWaitSetRunResult.AllEventsHandled.
